critical_code_review_comments: AttachmentUploader posts multipart via api.post with an explicit 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data' header — normally axios should let the browser set boundary automatically. If /api/media/upload ever rejects because the boundary isn't attached, remove the manual header. Currently works, so cosmetic only.

server.py UserOut declares 'portfolio: List[dict] = []' but UserUpdate uses Optional[List[dict]] and stores whatever the client sends — there is no server-side validation of {type in image|video|link}. A malicious client could store arbitrary dict shapes. Consider a small Pydantic sub-model.

JobCreate.employment_type is a free-form str; recommend Literal['on_demand','temp','employee'] to reject typos at the API boundary (frontend currently sends only the 3 valid values, but any direct API call could store garbage).

OrderService.jsx now nears 775 lines with SERVICE_META + POPULAR_CATEGORIES + EMPLOYMENT_TYPES + step validators + JSX. Extraction of constants into /lib/orderMeta.js would help readability and enable reuse (Landing already duplicates icon meta).

ProviderMediaSection: portfolio is stored as {type: 'image'|'video'|'link', url, title?} but AttachmentUploader emits raw MIME types ('image/jpeg', 'video/mp4'). The reshape happens in onChange callback (line 214) — correct, but fragile: if AttachmentUploader ever stores files without a MIME (e.g. from URL import) they'll be classified as 'image'. Consider explicit kind detection.
